messages:
support-alex: Heads up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 latency spikes and a bunch of 429s on api.realtime.generate since ~2026-03-15T10:12Z. Sample req ids: req_9ab3, req_9ab4. Seeing admit_queue depth climb to ~1200. Can eng-sre take a look? @maria @raj

ops-bot: Alert: service api.realtime.generate p95 > 2.5s for 7m, error rate 5% (429). Metrics: http://grafana/redwood/d/something

maria: On it. Any recent deploys or config changes around 10:10Z?

support-alex: Customer timeline says started ~10:10Z. No deploys in support console for that window. Repro curl they used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime.generate 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer ****\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -H \"x-request-id: req_9ab3\" 
  -d '{\"model\":\"default-model-4g-conv\",\"input\":\"<long prompt here>\",\"max_tokens\":1024}' -v
```

raj: Looking at infra metrics: admission queue backlog spikes at 10:11Z. Worker pods report 0 free slots (concurrency exhausted). Per-token compute time normal (0.02s/token) — it's pre-serve queueing causing p95. Snippet from admission controller logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:11:08Z admit_controller INFO queued=1203 accept_rate=11/s concurrency_limit=200 fail_fast=false
2026-03-15T10:11:30Z admit_controller WARN queue_depth=1100 oldest_wait=34s
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z admit_controller INFO routing to fallback=false
```

maria: That concurrency_limit=200 looks suspicious. Was that changed recently?

deploy-bot: Config change recorded: route default-model-4g-conv concurrency_limit decreased from 250 -> 200 at 2026-03-15T09:59Z by katie (reason: cost cap).

katie: Yep, I reduced it as a cost optimization during a maintenance window. I didn't expect this traffic pattern. If this is the cause I can revert. @raj any quick mitigation suggestions?

raj: Short-term options: 1) increase concurrency_limit back to 300; 2) enable emergency burst capacity for this pool; 3) route heavy/long-seq requests to a proxy fallback model with more slots; 4) enable an admit-drop for extreme-length requests. Quickest is bumping concurrency and enabling fallback.

maria: Can we also detect extremely long seq_len requests and treat them as lower priority / backpressure? We're seeing some requests with seq_len=8192 and huge kv-cache allocations.

support-alex: We can ask affected customers to reduce batch size in the short term but need a platform-side fix ASAP. Several enterprise customers are hitting this.

raj: I'm going to bump concurrency to 300 and enable fallback routing for the route. Applying change now: PATCH /configs/routes/default-model-4g-conv {\"concurrency_limit\":300, \"fallback_enabled\":true}

ops-bot: Configuration update requested by raj at 2026-03-15T10:32Z: route-update default-model-4g-conv concurrency_limit=300 fallback_enabled=true

maria: Monitoring metrics and queue depth...

support-alex: Customer reported improvement — p95 down from ~3.1s to ~0.9s on their end at ~10:36Z. :thumbsup:

raj: Admission queue depth trending down: 1200 -> 120 -> 28 in ~4min. Error rate (429) back to 0.4%. Leaving the concurrency bump for 30m while we triage root cause.

maria: Immediate post-incident action items:
- revert/keep concurrency? keep at 300 for now and schedule a controlled rollback window.
- add synthetic test which simulates 1k concurrent long-seq requests to the route.
- add an alert rule: any manual reduction to concurrency_limit must create a high-severity ticket and require a 24h cooldown.
- consider auto-increase policy: if queue_depth > 500, auto-increase concurrency by +50 (cap 400) and enable fallback for 10m.

katie: That config change was part of a cost cap effort. My bad for not running a spike sim. Will coordinate with SRE before future reductions.

support-alex: I'll notify impacted customers and give repro + mitigation steps (we can include the curl snippet). Anyone want me to cc legal/support-ops on the email?

raj: Also adding immediate mitigation playbook to runbook: if admit_queue > 500 -> escalate to eng-sre, bump concurrency by 50, enable fallback routing, message customers. Will open RFC for automated policy.

maria: Filing incident ticket and postmortem template now (link placeholder: https://redwood.atlassian/INC-XXXX). Marking SEV-Medium due to customer impact.

deploy-bot: Rollback window: auto-rollback disabled; manual rollback window ends 2026-03-15T11:05Z.

katie: Will follow up with cost-team and propose alternative cost controls that don't reduce concurrency without simulation.

maria: Summary for postmortem: root cause = manual concurrency_limit reduction (250->200) + unexpected traffic spike with long-sequence requests causing queueing. Short-term fix = bumped concurrency to 300 + enabled fallback. Next steps = tests, alerts, playbook, RFC for auto-scale.

support-alex: Thanks team — I'll update affected customers and close the support escalation once postmortem link is up.
